<?xml-model href="./FactDictionaryModule.rng"?>
<!--
  Virginia resident return, tax year 2024: prototype rules, not a return. One of the Virginia
  modules (facts/virginia*.xml), loaded as one dictionary beside the federal modules; the
  Virginia README in docs/virginia/ lists them and docs/adr/003-the-layout-for-growth.md says
  why they are split. Every fact names its source: Va. Code Title 58.1, Chapter 3
  (https://law.lis.virginia.gov/vacode/title58.1/) and the 2024 Form 760 instructions. A module
  reads federal facts only through what the federal return exports to states
  (stateSystems="true") or to MeF (mef="true"); scripts/check-virginia-exports.py enforces it.

  This module: every tax-year figure, date and rate-schedule amount, one fact each with a
  <TaxYear> and its source. A rule in another module refers to a figure by
  <Dependency module="virginiaConstants" …>, and no <Day> or non-zero <Dollar> literal may appear
  outside this file (scripts/check-virginia-constants.py), so a new tax year is one edit in one file.
-->
<FactDictionaryModule>
  <Facts>



    <!-- ============ Figures for tax year 2024. One edit per year goes here. ============ -->
    <Fact path="/vaStandardDeductionSingle">
      <Name>Virginia standard deduction, Filing Status 1 and 3</Name>
      <Description>Va. Code § 58.1-322.03(1)(b): $8,500 for taxable years beginning 2024-01-01
        and before 2025-01-01 (single; married filing separately takes one-half of the married
        amount, also $8,500). 2024 Form 760 instructions, Line 11.</Description>
      <TaxYear>2024</TaxYear>
      <Derived><Dollar>8500</Dollar></Derived>
    </Fact>

    <Fact path="/vaStandardDeductionMarried">
      <Name>Virginia standard deduction, Filing Status 2</Name>
      <Description>Va. Code § 58.1-322.03(1)(b): $17,000 for married persons filing jointly,
        taxable year 2024. 2024 Form 760 instructions, Line 11.</Description>
      <TaxYear>2024</TaxYear>
      <Derived><Dollar>17000</Dollar></Derived>
    </Fact>

    <Fact path="/vaPersonalExemptionAmount">
      <Name>Virginia personal exemption</Name>
      <Description>Va. Code § 58.1-322.03(2)(a): $930 for each personal exemption allowable
        federally. 2024 Form 760 instructions, Exemptions Section A.</Description>
      <TaxYear>2024</TaxYear>
      <Derived><Dollar>930</Dollar></Derived>
    </Fact>

    <Fact path="/vaAgedOrBlindExemptionAmount">
      <Name>Virginia additional exemption, 65 or older or blind</Name>
      <Description>Va. Code § 58.1-322.03(2)(b): $800 for a taxpayer who is aged or blind under
        IRC § 63(f). 2024 Form 760 instructions, Exemptions Section B: 65 or older on or before
        January 1, 2025.</Description>
      <TaxYear>2024</TaxYear>
      <Derived><Dollar>800</Dollar></Derived>
    </Fact>

    <Fact path="/vaAgeDeductionMaximum">
      <Name>Virginia age deduction, maximum</Name>
      <Description>Va. Code § 58.1-322.03(5): $12,000 for each qualifying person. 2024 Form 760
        instructions, Line 4.</Description>
      <TaxYear>2024</TaxYear>
      <Derived><Dollar>12000</Dollar></Derived>
    </Fact>

    <Fact path="/vaAgeDeductionFullAmountBirthDateCutoff">
      <Name>Virginia age deduction, last birth date for the full amount</Name>
      <Description>Va. Code § 58.1-322.03(5)(a): born on or before January 1, 1939, the full
        $12,000 regardless of income. A statutory date, kept with the figures so the file holds
        no date literal outside this block.</Description>
      <TaxYear>2024</TaxYear>
      <Derived><Day>1939-01-01</Day></Derived>
    </Fact>

    <Fact path="/vaAgeDeductionIncomeThresholdSingle">
      <Name>Virginia age deduction income threshold, single</Name>
      <Description>Va. Code § 58.1-322.03(5)(b): the $12,000 is reduced $1 for each $1 of adjusted
        federal adjusted gross income over $50,000 for single taxpayers.</Description>
      <TaxYear>2024</TaxYear>
      <Derived><Dollar>50000</Dollar></Derived>
    </Fact>

    <Fact path="/vaAgeDeductionIncomeThresholdMarried">
      <Name>Virginia age deduction income threshold, married</Name>
      <Description>Va. Code § 58.1-322.03(5)(b): $75,000 for married taxpayers, measured on the
        joint AFAGI of both spouses.</Description>
      <TaxYear>2024</TaxYear>
      <Derived><Dollar>75000</Dollar></Derived>
    </Fact>

    <Fact path="/vaFilingThresholdSingle">
      <Name>Virginia filing threshold, single</Name>
      <Description>Va. Code § 58.1-321(A): no tax if Virginia adjusted gross income is less than
        $11,950 for a single individual (taxable years from 2012). 2024 Form 760 instructions,
        Line 9.</Description>
      <TaxYear>2024</TaxYear>
      <Derived><Dollar>11950</Dollar></Derived>
    </Fact>

    <Fact path="/vaFilingThresholdMarried">
      <Name>Virginia filing threshold, married</Name>
      <Description>Va. Code § 58.1-321(A): $23,900 for an individual and spouse (one-half for
        married filing separately; this prototype applies the joint figure to Filing Status 2
        only).</Description>
      <TaxYear>2024</TaxYear>
      <Derived><Dollar>23900</Dollar></Derived>
    </Fact>

    <Fact path="/vaRateScheduleBracket1Top">
      <Name>Rate schedule, top of the 2% bracket</Name>
      <Description>Va. Code § 58.1-320: 2% of income not exceeding $3,000 (taxable years from
        1990). 2024 Form 760 instructions, Tax Rate Schedule.</Description>
      <TaxYear>2024</TaxYear>
      <Derived><Dollar>3000</Dollar></Derived>
    </Fact>

    <Fact path="/vaRateScheduleBracket2Top">
      <Name>Rate schedule, top of the 3% bracket</Name>
      <Description>Va. Code § 58.1-320: 3% of income over $3,000 to $5,000.</Description>
      <TaxYear>2024</TaxYear>
      <Derived><Dollar>5000</Dollar></Derived>
    </Fact>

    <Fact path="/vaRateScheduleBracket3Top">
      <Name>Rate schedule, top of the 5% bracket</Name>
      <Description>Va. Code § 58.1-320: 5% of income over $5,000 to $17,000; 5.75% above.</Description>
      <TaxYear>2024</TaxYear>
      <Derived><Dollar>17000</Dollar></Derived>
    </Fact>

    <Fact path="/vaRateScheduleTaxAtBracket1Top">
      <Name>Rate schedule, tax at $3,000</Name>
      <Description>The cumulative figure the 2024 Form 760 instructions print: $60 at $3,000
        (2% of $3,000).</Description>
      <TaxYear>2024</TaxYear>
      <Derived><Dollar>60</Dollar></Derived>
    </Fact>

    <Fact path="/vaRateScheduleTaxAtBracket2Top">
      <Name>Rate schedule, tax at $5,000</Name>
      <Description>$120 at $5,000: $60 plus 3% of $2,000.</Description>
      <TaxYear>2024</TaxYear>
      <Derived><Dollar>120</Dollar></Derived>
    </Fact>

    <Fact path="/vaRateScheduleTaxAtBracket3Top">
      <Name>Rate schedule, tax at $17,000</Name>
      <Description>$720 at $17,000: $120 plus 5% of $12,000.</Description>
      <TaxYear>2024</TaxYear>
      <Derived><Dollar>720</Dollar></Derived>
    </Fact>

    <Fact path="/vaRateScheduleRate1">
      <Name>Rate schedule, first rate</Name>
      <Description>Va. Code § 58.1-320: 2% on income not exceeding $3,000.</Description>
      <TaxYear>2024</TaxYear>
      <Derived><Rational>2/100</Rational></Derived>
    </Fact>

    <Fact path="/vaRateScheduleRate2">
      <Name>Rate schedule, second rate</Name>
      <Description>Va. Code § 58.1-320: 3% on income over $3,000 to $5,000.</Description>
      <TaxYear>2024</TaxYear>
      <Derived><Rational>3/100</Rational></Derived>
    </Fact>

    <Fact path="/vaRateScheduleRate3">
      <Name>Rate schedule, third rate</Name>
      <Description>Va. Code § 58.1-320: 5% on income over $5,000 to $17,000.</Description>
      <TaxYear>2024</TaxYear>
      <Derived><Rational>5/100</Rational></Derived>
    </Fact>

    <Fact path="/vaRateScheduleRate4">
      <Name>Rate schedule, top rate</Name>
      <Description>Va. Code § 58.1-320: 5.75% on income over $17,000.</Description>
      <TaxYear>2024</TaxYear>
      <Derived><Rational>575/10000</Rational></Derived>
    </Fact>

    <Fact path="/vaLowIncomeCreditPerExemption">
      <Name>Credit for Low-Income Individuals, per exemption</Name>
      <Description>Va. Code § 58.1-339.8(B)(1): $300 each for the individual, the spouse and each dependent. 2024
        Form 760 instructions, Schedule ADJ Line 13.</Description>
      <TaxYear>2024</TaxYear>
      <Derived><Dollar>300</Dollar></Derived>
    </Fact>

    <Fact path="/vaPovertyGuidelineFirstPerson">
      <Name>Poverty guideline, a family of one</Name>
      <Description>2024 Form 760 instructions, Schedule ADJ Line 11, Poverty Guideline Table:
        $15,060 for one eligible exemption (the 2024 federal poverty guideline).</Description>
      <TaxYear>2024</TaxYear>
      <Derived><Dollar>15060</Dollar></Derived>
    </Fact>

    <Fact path="/vaPovertyGuidelineEachAdditionalPerson">
      <Name>Poverty guideline, each additional family member</Name>
      <Description>2024 Form 760 instructions, Poverty Guideline Table: $5,380 for each additional
        person, spouse and dependent exemption ($20,440 for two, $52,720 for eight).</Description>
      <TaxYear>2024</TaxYear>
      <Derived><Dollar>5380</Dollar></Derived>
    </Fact>

    <Fact path="/vaEarnedIncomeCreditRate">
      <Name>Virginia Earned Income Credit rate, nonrefundable</Name>
      <Description>Va. Code § 58.1-339.8(B)(2): 20% of the federal earned income credit, in place of the
        Credit for Low-Income Individuals. 2024 Form 760
        instructions, Schedule ADJ Line 15.</Description>
      <TaxYear>2024</TaxYear>
      <Derived><Rational>20/100</Rational></Derived>
    </Fact>

    <Fact path="/vaRefundableEarnedIncomeCreditRate">
      <Name>Refundable Virginia Earned Income Credit rate</Name>
      <Description>Va. Code § 58.1-339.8(B)(3)(a): for taxable years 2022 through 2024, 15% of the federal
        earned income credit, refundable, in place of either nonrefundable credit (20% from 2025,
        subdivision 3 b). 2024 Form 760
        instructions, Schedule ADJ Line 16b.</Description>
      <TaxYear>2024</TaxYear>
      <Derived><Rational>15/100</Rational></Derived>
    </Fact>

    <Fact path="/vaMilitaryBasicPayMaximum">
      <Name>Military basic pay subtraction, maximum</Name>
      <Description>Va. Code § 58.1-322.02(15): up to $15,000 of military basic pay, reduced $1 for
        each $1 of basic pay over $15,000, so nothing at $30,000 or more. 2024 Form 760
        instructions, Schedule ADJ subtraction code 38.</Description>
      <TaxYear>2024</TaxYear>
      <Derived><Dollar>15000</Dollar></Derived>
    </Fact>

    <Fact path="/vaMilitaryBenefitsMaximum">
      <Name>Military benefits subtraction, maximum</Name>
      <Description>Va. Code § 58.1-322.02(18)(c): $30,000 of military benefits for taxable year 2024
        ($40,000 from 2025), at any age; (18)(d) defines them as military retirement income, § 134
        qualified military benefits, and Survivor Benefit Plan and other military benefits paid to a
        surviving spouse. 2024 Form 760 instructions, Schedule ADJ subtraction code 60.</Description>
      <TaxYear>2024</TaxYear>
      <Derived><Dollar>30000</Dollar></Derived>
    </Fact>

    <Fact path="/vaCommonwealthSaversCap">
      <Name>Commonwealth Savers deduction cap</Name>
      <Description>Va. Code § 58.1-322.03(7)(a): "limited to $4,000 per prepaid tuition contract or college
        savings trust account" per return per taxable year. This prototype treats the contributions as
        one account; the carryforward of the excess to later years is out of scope.</Description>
      <TaxYear>2024</TaxYear>
      <Derived><Dollar>4000</Dollar></Derived>
    </Fact>

    <Fact path="/vaCommonwealthSaversAge70BirthDateCutoff">
      <Name>Commonwealth Savers, last birth date for the no-cap rule</Name>
      <Description>Va. Code § 58.1-322.03(7)(b): a contributor who has attained age 70 is not subject to
        the $4,000 limit. Born on or before December 31, 1954 has attained 70 during tax year 2024.</Description>
      <TaxYear>2024</TaxYear>
      <Derived><Day>1954-12-31</Day></Derived>
    </Fact>

  </Facts>
</FactDictionaryModule>
facts.virginiaCredits:
<?xml-model href="./FactDictionaryModule.rng"?>
<!--
  Virginia resident return, tax year 2024: prototype rules, not a return. One of the Virginia
  modules (facts/virginia*.xml), loaded as one dictionary beside the federal modules; the
  Virginia README in docs/virginia/ lists them and docs/adr/003-the-layout-for-growth.md says
  why they are split. Every fact names its source: Va. Code Title 58.1, Chapter 3
  (https://law.lis.virginia.gov/vacode/title58.1/) and the 2024 Form 760 instructions. A module
  reads federal facts only through what the federal return exports to states
  (stateSystems="true") or to MeF (mef="true"); scripts/check-virginia-exports.py enforces it.

  This module: Line 23, the three low-income credits (Va. Code § 58.1-339.8, Schedule ADJ Lines 10
  to 17), and the choice § 58.1-339.8(D) forces between a credit and the deductions it bars:
  /vaClaimsLowIncomeCredit, which the Form 760 line facts in the other modules switch on, and the
  facts the summary uses to say what was given up or passed over.
-->
<FactDictionaryModule>
  <Facts>


    <!-- ============ Line 23: the low-income credits, Schedule ADJ Lines 10 to 17. ============ -->

    <Fact path="/vaCanClaimLowIncomeCredit">
      <Name>Not barred from the low-income credits outright</Name>
      <Description>Va. Code § 58.1-339.8(B)(1) and the 2024 Schedule ADJ eligibility requirements: no
        credit for a filer claimed as a dependent on another return. The other bars (the age
        deduction, the 65 or older and blind exemptions, military basic pay, claimed by the filer or
        the spouse) are elections, weighed in /vaClaimsLowIncomeCredit. The National Guard and
        federal and state employee subtractions (codes 28 and 39) are out of scope, as is anything a
        dependent claims.</Description>
      <Derived>
        <Not><Dependency module="filers" path="/primaryFiler/canBeClaimed" /></Not>
      </Derived>
    </Fact>

    <Fact path="/vaPovertyGuideline">
      <Name>Schedule ADJ Line 11, poverty guideline for the family size</Name>
      <Description>2024 Poverty Guideline Table: $15,060 for one, plus $5,380 for each more person.
        Family size is the You, Spouse and Dependents count (/vaPersonalExemptionCount).</Description>
      <Derived>
        <Add>
          <Dependency module="virginiaConstants" path="/vaPovertyGuidelineFirstPerson" />
          <Multiply>
            <Dependency module="virginiaConstants" path="/vaPovertyGuidelineEachAdditionalPerson" />
            <Subtract>
              <Minuend><Dependency module="virginiaDeductions" path="/vaPersonalExemptionCount" /></Minuend>
              <Subtrahends><Int>1</Int></Subtrahends>
            </Subtract>
          </Multiply>
        </Add>
      </Derived>
    </Fact>

    <Fact path="/vaQualifiesForCreditForLowIncomeIndividuals">
      <Name>Family VAGI at or under the poverty guideline</Name>
      <Description>Va. Code § 58.1-339.8(B)(1). Family VAGI (Schedule ADJ Line 10) is the return's
        Virginia AGI with no age deduction or basic pay subtraction; a dependent's own income is not
        on the federal return, so it is taken as $0 here.</Description>
      <Derived>
        <All>
          <Dependency path="/vaCanClaimLowIncomeCredit" />
          <LessThanOrEqual>
            <Left><Dependency module="virginiaIncome" path="/vaWithCreditAdjustedGrossIncome" /></Left>
            <Right><Dependency path="/vaPovertyGuideline" /></Right>
          </LessThanOrEqual>
        </All>
      </Derived>
    </Fact>

    <Fact path="/vaCreditForLowIncomeIndividuals">
      <Name>Schedule ADJ Line 13, Credit for Low-Income Individuals</Name>
      <Description>Va. Code § 58.1-339.8(B)(1): $300 times the personal and dependent exemptions
        (Schedule ADJ Line 12; not the 65 or older or blind ones), if the family qualifies.</Description>
      <Derived>
        <Switch>
          <Case>
            <When><Dependency path="/vaQualifiesForCreditForLowIncomeIndividuals" /></When>
            <Then><Multiply>
                <Dependency module="virginiaConstants" path="/vaLowIncomeCreditPerExemption" />
                <Dependency module="virginiaDeductions" path="/vaPersonalExemptionCount" />
              </Multiply></Then>
          </Case>
          <Case>
            <When><True /></When>
            <Then><Dollar>0</Dollar></Then>
          </Case>
        </Switch>
      </Derived>
    </Fact>

    <Fact path="/vaFederalEarnedIncomeCredit">
      <Name>Schedule ADJ Line 14, federal earned income credit</Name>
      <Description>Read from the federal return (/earnedIncomeCredit, exported to MeF as Form 1040
        line 27). $0 for a filer claimed as a dependent.</Description>
      <Derived>
        <Switch>
          <Case>
            <When><Dependency path="/vaCanClaimLowIncomeCredit" /></When>
            <Then><Dependency module="eitc" path="/earnedIncomeCredit" /></Then>
          </Case>
          <Case>
            <When><True /></When>
            <Then><Dollar>0</Dollar></Then>
          </Case>
        </Switch>
      </Derived>
    </Fact>

    <Fact path="/vaEarnedIncomeCredit">
      <Name>Schedule ADJ Line 15, Virginia Earned Income Credit</Name>
      <Description>Va. Code § 58.1-339.8(B)(2): 20% of Line 14, rounded to the dollar.</Description>
      <Derived>
        <Round>
          <Multiply>
            <Dependency module="virginiaConstants" path="/vaEarnedIncomeCreditRate" />
            <Dependency path="/vaFederalEarnedIncomeCredit" />
          </Multiply>
        </Round>
      </Derived>
    </Fact>

    <Fact path="/vaGreaterNonrefundableCredit">
      <Name>Schedule ADJ Line 16a, the greater of Line 13 or Line 15</Name>
      <Description>Schedule ADJ Line 16a: the greater of Line 13 (the Credit for Low-Income Individuals) and Line 15 (the nonrefundable Virginia Earned Income Credit), § 58.1-339.8; the schedule claims one, not both.</Description>
      <Derived>
        <GreaterOf>
          <Dependency path="/vaCreditForLowIncomeIndividuals" />
          <Dependency path="/vaEarnedIncomeCredit" />
        </GreaterOf>
      </Derived>
    </Fact>

    <Fact path="/vaRefundableEarnedIncomeCredit">
      <Name>Schedule ADJ Line 16b, Refundable Virginia Earned Income Credit</Name>
      <Description>Va. Code § 58.1-339.8(B)(3)(a): 15% of Line 14, rounded to the dollar.</Description>
      <Derived>
        <Round>
          <Multiply>
            <Dependency module="virginiaConstants" path="/vaRefundableEarnedIncomeCreditRate" />
            <Dependency path="/vaFederalEarnedIncomeCredit" />
          </Multiply>
        </Round>
      </Derived>
    </Fact>

    <Fact path="/vaNonrefundableCreditUsable">
      <Name>Line 16a, limited to the tax</Name>
      <Description>Va. Code § 58.1-339.8(C): a nonrefundable credit cannot exceed the tax (Line 18,
        here the tax on the return that claims the credit).</Description>
      <Derived>
        <LesserOf>
          <Dependency path="/vaGreaterNonrefundableCredit" />
          <Dependency module="virginiaTax" path="/vaWithCreditTax" />
        </LesserOf>
      </Derived>
    </Fact>

    <Fact path="/vaCreditIsRefundable">
      <Name>The refundable credit is worth more than the nonrefundable one</Name>
      <Description>2024 Schedule ADJ Line 17: "Choose the credit option that benefits you the most."</Description>
      <Derived>
        <GreaterThan>
          <Left><Dependency path="/vaRefundableEarnedIncomeCredit" /></Left>
          <Right><Dependency path="/vaNonrefundableCreditUsable" /></Right>
        </GreaterThan>
      </Derived>
    </Fact>

    <Fact path="/vaBestLowIncomeCredit">
      <Name>Schedule ADJ Line 17, the credit that benefits the filer most</Name>
      <Description>The lesser of Line 16a and the tax, or Line 16b, whichever is greater.</Description>
      <Derived>
        <GreaterOf>
          <Dependency path="/vaNonrefundableCreditUsable" />
          <Dependency path="/vaRefundableEarnedIncomeCredit" />
        </GreaterOf>
      </Derived>
    </Fact>

    <Fact path="/vaWithCreditTaxAfterCredit">
      <Name>Tax less the credit, if the return claims a low-income credit</Name>
      <Description>Negative when the refundable credit exceeds the tax.</Description>
      <Derived>
        <Subtract>
          <Minuend><Dependency module="virginiaTax" path="/vaWithCreditTax" /></Minuend>
          <Subtrahends><Dependency path="/vaBestLowIncomeCredit" /></Subtrahends>
        </Subtract>
      </Derived>
    </Fact>

    <Fact path="/vaClaimsLowIncomeCredit">
      <Name>The return claims a low-income credit</Name>
      <Description>The election Form 760 leaves to the filer: the instructions for Line 4 say to
        "claim the deduction or subtraction that gives you the greatest tax benefit." The return
        claims a credit when there is one and the tax less the credit is lower than the tax keeping
        everything Va. Code § 58.1-339.8(D) says the filer, the spouse or both would give up: the age
        deduction of either spouse, the 65 or older and blind exemptions of either spouse, and the
        military basic pay subtraction. Withholding, payments and use tax are the same either way, so
        this is the whole comparison.</Description>
      <Derived>
        <All>
          <GreaterThan>
            <Left><Dependency path="/vaBestLowIncomeCredit" /></Left>
            <Right><Dollar>0</Dollar></Right>
          </GreaterThan>
          <LessThan>
            <Left><Dependency path="/vaWithCreditTaxAfterCredit" /></Left>
            <Right><Dependency module="virginiaTax" path="/vaWithoutCreditTax" /></Right>
          </LessThan>
        </All>
      </Derived>
    </Fact>

    <Fact path="/vaLowIncomeCredit">
      <Name>Form 760 Line 23, Credit for Low-Income Individuals or Virginia Earned Income Credit</Name>
      <Description>Schedule ADJ Line 17 when the return claims it; otherwise $0.</Description>
      <Derived>
        <Switch>
          <Case>
            <When><Dependency path="/vaClaimsLowIncomeCredit" /></When>
            <Then><Dependency path="/vaBestLowIncomeCredit" /></Then>
          </Case>
          <Case>
            <When><True /></When>
            <Then><Dollar>0</Dollar></Then>
          </Case>
        </Switch>
      </Derived>
    </Fact>

    <Fact path="/vaClaimsRefundableEarnedIncomeCredit">
      <Name>Line 23 is the Refundable Virginia Earned Income Credit</Name>
      <Description>Which credit Line 23 is, for the summary's words: the refundable Virginia Earned Income Credit (Schedule ADJ Line 16b, § 58.1-339.8), when the return claims a low-income credit and /vaCreditIsRefundable chose the refundable one.</Description>
      <Derived>
        <All>
          <Dependency path="/vaClaimsLowIncomeCredit" />
          <Dependency path="/vaCreditIsRefundable" />
        </All>
      </Derived>
    </Fact>

    <Fact path="/vaClaimsCreditForLowIncomeIndividuals">
      <Name>Line 23 is the Credit for Low-Income Individuals</Name>
      <Description>Line 16a is Line 13 when Line 13 is at least Line 15.</Description>
      <Derived>
        <All>
          <Dependency path="/vaClaimsLowIncomeCredit" />
          <Not><Dependency path="/vaCreditIsRefundable" /></Not>
          <GreaterThanOrEqual>
            <Left><Dependency path="/vaCreditForLowIncomeIndividuals" /></Left>
            <Right><Dependency path="/vaEarnedIncomeCredit" /></Right>
          </GreaterThanOrEqual>
        </All>
      </Derived>
    </Fact>

    <Fact path="/vaClaimsNonrefundableEarnedIncomeCredit">
      <Name>Line 23 is the nonrefundable Virginia Earned Income Credit</Name>
      <Description>Which credit Line 23 is, for the summary's words: the nonrefundable Virginia Earned Income Credit (Schedule ADJ Line 15, § 58.1-339.8), when the return claims a low-income credit, the refundable one is not worth more, and Line 15 beats Line 13.</Description>
      <Derived>
        <All>
          <Dependency path="/vaClaimsLowIncomeCredit" />
          <Not><Dependency path="/vaCreditIsRefundable" /></Not>
          <Not><Dependency path="/vaClaimsCreditForLowIncomeIndividuals" /></Not>
        </All>
      </Derived>
    </Fact>

    <Fact path="/vaCreditReplacedAgeDeduction">
      <Name>Claiming the credit gave up the age deduction</Name>
      <Description>Shown on the summary, so the filer sees what the credit replaced and what it was
        worth; on a joint return the figure includes the spouse's deduction.</Description>
      <Derived>
        <All>
          <Dependency path="/vaClaimsLowIncomeCredit" />
          <GreaterThan>
            <Left><Dependency module="virginiaIncome" path="/vaAgeDeductionAllowed" /></Left>
            <Right><Dollar>0</Dollar></Right>
          </GreaterThan>
        </All>
      </Derived>
    </Fact>

    <Fact path="/vaCreditReplacedAgedOrBlindExemptions">
      <Name>Claiming the credit gave up the 65 or older or blind exemptions</Name>
      <Description>Shown on the summary, so the filer sees what the credit replaced and what it was
        worth; on a joint return the figure includes the spouse's boxes.</Description>
      <Derived>
        <All>
          <Dependency path="/vaClaimsLowIncomeCredit" />
          <GreaterThan>
            <Left><Dependency module="virginiaDeductions" path="/vaAgedOrBlindExemptionsAllowed" /></Left>
            <Right><Dollar>0</Dollar></Right>
          </GreaterThan>
        </All>
      </Derived>
    </Fact>

    <Fact path="/vaCreditReplacedMilitaryBasicPay">
      <Name>Claiming the credit gave up the military basic pay subtraction</Name>
      <Description>Shown on the summary, so the filer sees what the credit replaced and what it was worth.</Description>
      <Derived>
        <All>
          <Dependency path="/vaClaimsLowIncomeCredit" />
          <GreaterThan>
            <Left><Dependency module="virginiaIncome" path="/vaMilitaryBasicPaySubtractionAllowed" /></Left>
            <Right><Dollar>0</Dollar></Right>
          </GreaterThan>
        </All>
      </Derived>
    </Fact>

    <Fact path="/vaCreditDeclinedForADeduction">
      <Name>A credit was available, but keeping the deductions saves more</Name>

Computes no line.</Description>

        <All>
          <Not><Dependency path="/vaClaimsLowIncomeCredit" /></Not>
          <GreaterThan>

facts.virginiaDeductions:
<?xml-model href="./FactDictionaryModule.rng"?>
<!--
  Virginia resident return, tax year 2024: prototype rules, not a return. One of the Virginia
  modules (facts/virginia*.xml), loaded as one dictionary beside the federal modules; the
  Virginia README in docs/virginia/ lists them and docs/adr/003-the-layout-for-growth.md says
  why they are split. Every fact names its source: Va. Code Title 58.1, Chapter 3
  (https://law.lis.virginia.gov/vacode/title58.1/) and the 2024 Form 760 instructions. A module
  reads federal facts only through what the federal return exports to states
  (stateSystems="true") or to MeF (mef="true"); scripts/check-virginia-exports.py enforces it.

  This module: Lines 11 to 15, the standard deduction, exemptions, the Commonwealth Savers
  deduction (Line 13, the one deduction only the filer can report) and taxable income, each
  computed both ways (see virginiaIncome.xml).
-->
<FactDictionaryModule>
  <Facts>


    <!-- ============ Lines 11 to 15: deductions, exemptions, taxable income. ============ -->

    <Fact path="/vaStandardDeductionForFilingStatus">
      <Name>Standard deduction amount for this filing status</Name>
      <Description>Va. Code § 58.1-322.03(1)(b). Federal itemizers must itemize in Virginia (Line
        10); that case is out of scope, so every return here takes the standard deduction.</Description>
      <Derived>
        <Switch>
          <Case>
            <When><Dependency module="virginiaFiler" path="/vaIsFilingStatus2" /></When>
            <Then><Dependency module="virginiaConstants" path="/vaStandardDeductionMarried" /></Then>
          </Case>
          <Case>
            <When><True /></When>
            <Then><Dependency module="virginiaConstants" path="/vaStandardDeductionSingle" /></Then>
          </Case>
        </Switch>
      </Derived>
    </Fact>

    <Fact path="/vaStandardDeduction">
      <Name>Form 760 Line 11, standard deduction</Name>
      <Description>Va. Code § 58.1-322.03(1)(b): a person who can be claimed as a dependent on
        another's return takes the deduction only with respect to earned income; 2024 Form 760
        instructions, Line 11, "Dependent on Another's Return": the smaller of earned income and
        the standard deduction. Earned income here is W-2 wages (/wages, exported to MeF).</Description>
      <Derived>
        <Switch>
          <Case>
            <When><Dependency module="filers" path="/primaryFiler/canBeClaimed" /></When>
            <Then>
              <LesserOf>
                <Dependency path="/vaStandardDeductionForFilingStatus" />
                <Dependency module="formW2s" path="/wages" />
              </LesserOf>
            </Then>
          </Case>
          <Case>
            <When><True /></When>
            <Then><Dependency path="/vaStandardDeductionForFilingStatus" /></Then>
          </Case>
        </Switch>
      </Derived>
    </Fact>

    <Fact path="/vaPersonalExemptionCount">
      <Name>Exemptions claimed in the You, Spouse and Dependents boxes</Name>
      <Description>2024 Form 760 instructions, Exemptions Section A: yourself, your spouse on a
        joint return, and the dependents claimed federally, counted from each household member's
        isClaimedDependent, which the federal return exports to states. (The federal
        /claimedDependentsCount is not exported, so it is not read.)</Description>
      <Derived>
        <Add>
          <Int>1</Int>
          <Switch>
            <Case>
              <When><Dependency module="virginiaFiler" path="/vaIsFilingStatus2" /></When>
              <Then><Int>1</Int></Then>
            </Case>
            <Case>
              <When><True /></When>
              <Then><Int>0</Int></Then>
            </Case>
          </Switch>
          <Count>
            <Dependency module="familyAndHousehold" path="/familyAndHousehold/*/isClaimedDependent" />
          </Count>
        </Add>
      </Derived>
    </Fact>

    <Fact path="/vaAgedOrBlindExemptionCount">
      <Name>Exemptions claimed in the 65 or older and Blind boxes</Name>
      <Description>2024 Form 760 instructions, Exemptions Section B, four boxes: you 65 or older on or
        before January 1, 2025 (the federal /age65OrOlder rule), you blind for federal purposes, and
        on a joint return the same two for your spouse.</Description>
      <Derived>
        <Add>
          <Switch>
            <Case>
              <When><Dependency module="filers" path="/primaryFiler/age65OrOlder" /></When>
              <Then><Int>1</Int></Then>
            </Case>
            <Case>
              <When><True /></When>
              <Then><Int>0</Int></Then>
            </Case>
          </Switch>
          <Switch>
            <Case>
              <When><Dependency module="filers" path="/primaryFiler/isBlind" /></When>
              <Then><Int>1</Int></Then>
            </Case>
            <Case>
              <When><True /></When>
              <Then><Int>0</Int></Then>
            </Case>
          </Switch>
          <Switch>
            <Case>
              <When><Dependency module="virginiaFiler" path="/vaSpouseAge65OrOlder" /></When>
              <Then><Int>1</Int></Then>
            </Case>
            <Case>
              <When><True /></When>
              <Then><Int>0</Int></Then>
            </Case>
          </Switch>
          <Switch>
            <Case>
              <When><Dependency module="virginiaFiler" path="/vaSpouseIsBlind" /></When>
              <Then><Int>1</Int></Then>
            </Case>
            <Case>
              <When><True /></When>
              <Then><Int>0</Int></Then>
            </Case>
          </Switch>
        </Add>
      </Derived>
    </Fact>

    <Fact path="/vaPersonalExemptions">
      <Name>Exemptions, Section A amount</Name>
      <Description>Va. Code § 58.1-322.03(2)(a): $930 times the You, Spouse and Dependents count.</Description>
      <Derived>
        <Multiply>
          <Dependency module="virginiaConstants" path="/vaPersonalExemptionAmount" />
          <Dependency path="/vaPersonalExemptionCount" />
        </Multiply>
      </Derived>
    </Fact>

    <Fact path="/vaAgedOrBlindExemptionsAllowed">
      <Name>Exemptions, Section B amount the filers qualify for</Name>
      <Description>Va. Code § 58.1-322.03(2)(b): $800 times the 65 or older and Blind count, the
        spouse's boxes included. 2024 Form 760 instructions, Exemptions: these cannot be claimed with
        a Credit for Low-Income Individuals on Line 23 (Va. Code § 58.1-339.8(D)(4) bars every
        low-income credit when the filer or the spouse claims one).</Description>
      <Derived>
        <Multiply>
          <Dependency module="virginiaConstants" path="/vaAgedOrBlindExemptionAmount" />
          <Dependency path="/vaAgedOrBlindExemptionCount" />
        </Multiply>
      </Derived>
    </Fact>

    <Fact path="/vaWithoutCreditExemptions">
      <Name>Line 12 if the return keeps the 65 or older and blind exemptions</Name>
      <Description>Line 12 as it stands when no low-income credit is claimed: the personal exemptions plus the 65-or-older and blind exemptions, § 58.1-322.03(2). The credits module's switch picks this or the personal exemptions alone.</Description>
      <Derived>
        <Add>
          <Dependency path="/vaPersonalExemptions" />
          <Dependency path="/vaAgedOrBlindExemptionsAllowed" />
        </Add>
      </Derived>
    </Fact>

    <Fact path="/vaExemptions">
      <Name>Form 760 Line 12, exemptions</Name>
      <Description>Va. Code § 58.1-322.03(2): Section A plus Section B, or Section A alone when the
        return claims a low-income credit.</Description>
      <Derived>
        <Switch>
          <Case>
            <When><Dependency module="virginiaCredits" path="/vaClaimsLowIncomeCredit" /></When>
            <Then><Dependency path="/vaPersonalExemptions" /></Then>
          </Case>
          <Case>
            <When><True /></When>
            <Then><Dependency path="/vaWithoutCreditExemptions" /></Then>
          </Case>
        </Switch>
      </Derived>
    </Fact>

    <Fact path="/vaWithoutCreditTotalDeductions">
      <Name>Line 14 if the return keeps the 65 or older and blind exemptions</Name>
      <Description>Line 14 as it stands when no low-income credit is claimed: the standard deduction, both kinds of exemption and the Commonwealth Savers deduction. /vaTotalDeductions picks this or /vaWithCreditTotalDeductions.</Description>
      <Derived>
        <Add>
          <Dependency path="/vaStandardDeduction" />
          <Dependency path="/vaWithoutCreditExemptions" />
          <Dependency path="/vaCommonwealthSaversDeduction" />
        </Add>
      </Derived>
    </Fact>

    <Fact path="/vaWithCreditTotalDeductions">
      <Name>Line 14 if the return claims a low-income credit</Name>
      <Description>Line 14 as it stands when a low-income credit is claimed: the standard deduction, the personal exemptions alone (the credit bars the 65-or-older and blind exemptions, § 58.1-339.8(D)) and the Commonwealth Savers deduction.</Description>
      <Derived>
        <Add>
          <Dependency path="/vaStandardDeduction" />
          <Dependency path="/vaPersonalExemptions" />
          <Dependency path="/vaCommonwealthSaversDeduction" />
        </Add>
      </Derived>
    </Fact>

    <Fact path="/vaTotalDeductions">
      <Name>Form 760 Line 14, total deductions</Name>
      <Description>Lines 10 + 11 + 12 + 13, whichever way the return files. Line 10 (itemized) and
        the Schedule ADJ deductions other than Commonwealth Savers are out of scope and taken as $0.</Description>
      <Derived>
        <Switch>
          <Case>
            <When><Dependency module="virginiaCredits" path="/vaClaimsLowIncomeCredit" /></When>
            <Then><Dependency path="/vaWithCreditTotalDeductions" /></Then>
          </Case>
          <Case>
            <When><True /></When>
            <Then><Dependency path="/vaWithoutCreditTotalDeductions" /></Then>
          </Case>
        </Switch>
      </Derived>
    </Fact>

    <Fact path="/vaWithoutCreditTaxableIncome">
      <Name>Line 15 if the return keeps the age deduction and exemptions</Name>
      <Description>Line 9 minus Line 14, not below zero.</Description>
      <Derived>
        <GreaterOf>
          <Dollar>0</Dollar>
          <Subtract>
            <Minuend><Dependency module="virginiaIncome" path="/vaWithoutCreditAdjustedGrossIncome" /></Minuend>
            <Subtrahends><Dependency path="/vaWithoutCreditTotalDeductions" /></Subtrahends>
          </Subtract>
        </GreaterOf>
      </Derived>
    </Fact>

    <Fact path="/vaWithCreditTaxableIncome">
      <Name>Line 15 if the return claims a low-income credit</Name>
      <Description>Line 9 minus Line 14, not below zero.</Description>
      <Derived>
        <GreaterOf>
          <Dollar>0</Dollar>
          <Subtract>
            <Minuend><Dependency module="virginiaIncome" path="/vaWithCreditAdjustedGrossIncome" /></Minuend>
            <Subtrahends><Dependency path="/vaWithCreditTotalDeductions" /></Subtrahends>
          </Subtract>
        </GreaterOf>
      </Derived>
    </Fact>

    <Fact path="/vaTaxableIncome">
      <Name>Form 760 Line 15, Virginia taxable income</Name>
      <Description>Line 9 minus Line 14, not below zero.</Description>
      <Derived>
        <Switch>
          <Case>
            <When><Dependency module="virginiaCredits" path="/vaClaimsLowIncomeCredit" /></When>
            <Then><Dependency path="/vaWithCreditTaxableIncome" /></Then>
          </Case>
          <Case>
            <When><True /></When>
            <Then><Dependency path="/vaWithoutCreditTaxableIncome" /></Then>
          </Case>
        </Switch>
      </Derived>
    </Fact>

    <!-- ============ One thing only the filer knows: Line 13. ============ -->

    <Fact path="/vaHasCommonwealthSaversContributions">
      <Name>Contributed to a Commonwealth Savers (Virginia529) account in 2024</Name>
      <Description>Asked, because the plan reports nothing to the IRS. Va. Code § 58.1-322.03(7).</Description>
      <Writable><Boolean /></Writable>
    </Fact>

    <Fact path="/vaCommonwealthSaversContributions">
      <Name>Amount contributed to Commonwealth Savers accounts in 2024</Name>
      <Description>The total paid or contributed in the year, before the per-account cap.</Description>
      <Writable><Dollar /></Writable>
      <Placeholder><Dollar>0</Dollar></Placeholder>
    </Fact>

    <Fact path="/vaPrimaryFilerAge70OrOlder">
      <Name>Primary filer has attained age 70</Name>
      <Description>Va. Code § 58.1-322.03(7)(b): a contributor who has attained age 70 is not subject to the
        $4,000 limit. Born on or before December 31, 1954 for tax year 2024
        (/vaCommonwealthSaversAge70BirthDateCutoff). Reads the exported date of birth. The
        contributions are asked of the primary filer only, so the spouse's age does not enter.</Description>
      <Derived>
        <LessThanOrEqual>
          <Left><Dependency module="filers" path="/primaryFiler/dateOfBirth" /></Left>
          <Right><Dependency module="virginiaConstants" path="/vaCommonwealthSaversAge70BirthDateCutoff" /></Right>
        </LessThanOrEqual>
      </Derived>
    </Fact>

    <Fact path="/vaCommonwealthSaversDeduction">
      <Name>Form 760 Line 13 (Schedule ADJ), Commonwealth Savers deduction</Name>
      <Description>Va. Code § 58.1-322.03(7): the contribution, capped at $4,000 unless the filer has
        attained age 70. The other Schedule ADJ deductions are out of scope.</Description>
      <Derived>
        <Switch>
          <Case>
            <When><Not><Dependency path="/vaHasCommonwealthSaversContributions" /></Not></When>
            <Then><Dollar>0</Dollar></Then>
          </Case>
          <Case>
            <When><Dependency path="/vaPrimaryFilerAge70OrOlder" /></When>
            <Then><Dependency path="/vaCommonwealthSaversContributions" /></Then>
          </Case>
          <Case>
            <When><True /></When>
            <Then>
              <LesserOf>
                <Dependency module="virginiaConstants" path="/vaCommonwealthSaversCap" />
                <Dependency path="/vaCommonwealthSaversContributions" />
              </LesserOf>
            </Then>
          </Case>
        </Switch>
      </Derived>
    </Fact>

  </Facts>
</FactDictionaryModule>
facts.virginiaFiler:
<?xml-model href="./FactDictionaryModule.rng"?>
<!--
  Virginia resident return, tax year 2024: prototype rules, not a return. One of the Virginia
  modules (facts/virginia*.xml), loaded as one dictionary beside the federal modules; the
  Virginia README in docs/virginia/ lists them and docs/adr/003-the-layout-for-growth.md says
  why they are split. Every fact names its source: Va. Code Title 58.1, Chapter 3
  (https://law.lis.virginia.gov/vacode/title58.1/) and the 2024 Form 760 instructions. A module
  reads federal facts only through what the federal return exports to states
  (stateSystems="true") or to MeF (mef="true"); scripts/check-virginia-exports.py enforces it.

  This module: the residency gate, the Form 760 filing status, and the spouse on a joint return,
  found from the exported isPrimaryFiler flag because /secondaryFiler is not exported.
-->
<FactDictionaryModule>
  <Facts>


    <!-- ============ Residency: the gate. Reads the federal residency answer. ============ -->

    <Fact path="/vaIsResident">
      <Name>Virginia resident</Name>
      <Description>The filer lived in Virginia for all of the tax year, as answered on the federal
        residence question (/filerResidenceAndIncomeState, with 'va' added to the federal
        /scopedStateOptions). Part-year and nonresident returns (Forms 760PY and 763) are out of
        scope. This fact gates the Virginia screens; it is not an export.</Description>
      <Derived>
        <Equal>
          <Left><Dependency module="filers" path="/filerResidenceAndIncomeState" /></Left>
          <Right><Enum optionsPath="/scopedStateOptions">va</Enum></Right>
        </Equal>
      </Derived>
    </Fact>

    <!-- ============ Filing status, mapped to Form 760's three statuses. ============ -->

    <Fact path="/vaIsFilingStatus2">
      <Name>Virginia Filing Status 2, married filing jointly</Name>
      <Description>Form 760 Filing Status 2 corresponds to a federal joint return. Federal single
        and head of household file as Filing Status 1; married filing separately as Status 3.
        Qualifying surviving spouse is out of scope and treated as Status 1 here.</Description>
      <Derived>
        <Equal>
          <Left><Dependency module="filingStatus" path="/filingStatus" /></Left>
          <Right><Enum optionsPath="/filingStatusOptions">marriedFilingJointly</Enum></Right>
        </Equal>
      </Derived>
    </Fact>

    <!-- ============ The spouse on a joint return. ============ -->

    <Fact path="/filers/*/vaIsSpouse">
      <Name>This filer is the spouse</Name>
      <Description>Not the primary filer. The federal return exports each filer's
        /filers/*/isPrimaryFiler to states; the federal /filers/*/isSecondaryFiler and the
        /secondaryFiler pointer are not exported, so the spouse is found from the flag a state is
        handed.</Description>
      <Derived>
        <Not><Dependency module="filers" path="../isPrimaryFiler" /></Not>
      </Derived>
    </Fact>

    <Fact path="/vaSpouse">
      <Name>The spouse on a joint return</Name>
      <Description>The filer who is not the primary filer: how a state's software finds the spouse in
        what it is handed. Read only on Filing Status 2; the facts below guard that.</Description>
      <Derived>
        <Find path="/filers">
          <Dependency path="vaIsSpouse" />
        </Find>
      </Derived>
    </Fact>

    <Fact path="/vaSpouseAge65OrOlder">
      <Name>Spouse 65 or older</Name>
      <Description>On a joint return, the spouse's federal /age65OrOlder (65 on or before January 1,
        2025, the rule Virginia's Section B uses). False on any other filing status. A joint return
        always carries the spouse's date of birth, so the completeness guard only keeps a return with
        no spouse facts from going incomplete.</Description>
      <Derived>
        <Switch>
          <Case>
            <When><Dependency path="/vaIsFilingStatus2" /></When>
            <Then>
              <All>
                <IsComplete><Dependency module="filers" path="/vaSpouse/age65OrOlder" /></IsComplete>
                <Dependency module="filers" path="/vaSpouse/age65OrOlder" />
              </All>
            </Then>
          </Case>
          <Case>
            <When><True /></When>
            <Then><False /></Then>
          </Case>
        </Switch>
      </Derived>
    </Fact>

    <Fact path="/vaSpouseIsBlind">
      <Name>Spouse blind</Name>
      <Description>On a joint return, the spouse's federal /isBlind (blind for federal purposes, IRC
        § 63(f)). False on any other filing status.</Description>
      <Derived>
        <Switch>
          <Case>
            <When><Dependency path="/vaIsFilingStatus2" /></When>
            <Then>
              <All>
                <IsComplete><Dependency module="filers" path="/vaSpouse/isBlind" /></IsComplete>
                <Dependency module="filers" path="/vaSpouse/isBlind" />
              </All>
            </Then>
          </Case>
          <Case>
            <When><True /></When>
            <Then><False /></Then>
          </Case>
        </Switch>
      </Derived>
    </Fact>

    <Fact path="/vaSpouseBornOnOrBefore1939">
      <Name>Spouse born on or before January 1, 1939</Name>
      <Description>Va. Code § 58.1-322.03(5)(a), for the spouse on a joint return: the full $12,000 age
        deduction regardless of income. Reads the spouse's exported date of birth.</Description>
      <Derived>
        <Switch>
          <Case>
            <When><Dependency path="/vaIsFilingStatus2" /></When>
            <Then>
              <All>
                <IsComplete><Dependency module="filers" path="/vaSpouse/dateOfBirth" /></IsComplete>
                <LessThanOrEqual>
                  <Left><Dependency module="filers" path="/vaSpouse/dateOfBirth" /></Left>
                  <Right><Dependency module="virginiaConstants" path="/vaAgeDeductionFullAmountBirthDateCutoff" /></Right>
                </LessThanOrEqual>
              </All>
            </Then>
          </Case>
          <Case>
            <When><True /></When>
            <Then><False /></Then>
          </Case>
        </Switch>
      </Derived>
    </Fact>

  </Facts>
</FactDictionaryModule>
facts.virginiaIncome:
<?xml-model href="./FactDictionaryModule.rng"?>
<!--
  Virginia resident return, tax year 2024: prototype rules, not a return. One of the Virginia
  modules (facts/virginia*.xml), loaded as one dictionary beside the federal modules; the
  Virginia README in docs/virginia/ lists them and docs/adr/003-the-layout-for-growth.md says
  why they are split. Every fact names its source: Va. Code Title 58.1, Chapter 3
  (https://law.lis.virginia.gov/vacode/title58.1/) and the 2024 Form 760 instructions. A module
  reads federal facts only through what the federal return exports to states
  (stateSystems="true") or to MeF (mef="true"); scripts/check-virginia-exports.py enforces it.

  This module: Form 760 Lines 1 to 9, from federal AGI to Virginia AGI: the age deduction, the
  Schedule ADJ subtractions (military basic pay and benefits, unemployment), the filing threshold.
  Lines 4 to 9 are computed both keeping the deductions a low-income credit bars and giving them
  up (/vaWithoutCredit…, /vaWithCredit…); the Form 760 line facts switch on
  /vaClaimsLowIncomeCredit from virginiaCredits.xml.
-->
<FactDictionaryModule>
  <Facts>


    <!-- ============ Form 760 Lines 1 to 9: from federal AGI to Virginia AGI. ============ -->

    <Fact path="/vaFederalAdjustedGrossIncome">
      <Name>Form 760 Line 1, federal adjusted gross income</Name>
      <Description>Read from the federal return (/agi, exported to MeF as Form 1040 line 11).
        Line 2 (additions) is out of scope, so Line 3 equals Line 1.</Description>
      <Derived><Dependency module="taxCalculations" path="/agi" /></Derived>
    </Fact>

    <Fact path="/vaTaxableSocialSecurityBenefits">
      <Name>Form 760 Line 5, taxable Social Security benefits</Name>
      <Description>Va. Code § 58.1-322.02(3): benefits under Title II of the Social Security Act
        included in federal AGI are subtracted. Read from the federal return (Form 1040 line
        6b).</Description>
      <Derived><Dependency module="socialSecurity" path="/taxableSocialSecurityBenefits" /></Derived>
    </Fact>

    <Fact path="/vaAdjustedFederalAdjustedGrossIncome">
      <Name>Adjusted federal adjusted gross income (AFAGI)</Name>
      <Description>Va. Code § 58.1-322.03(5)(b): federal AGI minus Social Security Title II benefits
        and other benefits taxable solely under IRC § 86. Used only for the age deduction's
        income test; on a joint return it is the joint figure. 2024 Form 760 instructions, Age
        Deduction Worksheet lines 2 to 8 (the conformity addition and subtraction on worksheet
        lines 3 and 5 are out of scope).</Description>
      <Derived>
        <Subtract>
          <Minuend><Dependency path="/vaFederalAdjustedGrossIncome" /></Minuend>
          <Subtrahends><Dependency path="/vaTaxableSocialSecurityBenefits" /></Subtrahends>
        </Subtract>
      </Derived>
    </Fact>

    <Fact path="/vaPrimaryFilerBornOnOrBefore1939">
      <Name>Primary filer born on or before January 1, 1939</Name>
      <Description>Va. Code § 58.1-322.03(5)(a): the full $12,000 age deduction regardless of
        income. Reads the filer's date of birth, which the federal return exports to
        states.</Description>
      <Derived>
        <LessThanOrEqual>
          <Left><Dependency module="filers" path="/primaryFiler/dateOfBirth" /></Left>
          <Right><Dependency module="virginiaConstants" path="/vaAgeDeductionFullAmountBirthDateCutoff" /></Right>
        </LessThanOrEqual>
      </Derived>
    </Fact>

    <Fact path="/vaPrimaryFilerQualifiesForIncomeBasedAgeDeduction">
      <Name>Primary filer qualifies for the income-based age deduction</Name>
      <Description>Va. Code § 58.1-322.03(5)(b): born after January 1, 1939, and 65 or older. The
        federal /age65OrOlder uses the same rule as Virginia's instructions (65 on or before
        January 1 of the following year), so for tax year 2024 it means born on or before
        January 1, 1960.</Description>
      <Derived>
        <All>
          <Dependency module="filers" path="/primaryFiler/age65OrOlder" />
          <Not><Dependency path="/vaPrimaryFilerBornOnOrBefore1939" /></Not>
        </All>
      </Derived>
    </Fact>

    <Fact path="/vaSpouseQualifiesForIncomeBasedAgeDeduction">
      <Name>Spouse qualifies for the income-based age deduction</Name>
      <Description>Va. Code § 58.1-322.03(5)(b), for the spouse on a joint return: born after
        January 1, 1939, and 65 or older.</Description>
      <Derived>
        <All>
          <Dependency module="virginiaFiler" path="/vaSpouseAge65OrOlder" />
          <Not><Dependency module="virginiaFiler" path="/vaSpouseBornOnOrBefore1939" /></Not>
        </All>
      </Derived>
    </Fact>

    <Fact path="/vaAgeDeductionIncomeThreshold">
      <Name>Age deduction income threshold for this return</Name>
      <Description>Va. Code § 58.1-322.03(5)(b): $50,000 single, $75,000 married.</Description>
      <Derived>
        <Switch>
          <Case>
            <When><Dependency module="virginiaFiler" path="/vaIsFilingStatus2" /></When>
            <Then><Dependency module="virginiaConstants" path="/vaAgeDeductionIncomeThresholdMarried" /></Then>
          </Case>
          <Case>
            <When><True /></When>
            <Then><Dependency module="virginiaConstants" path="/vaAgeDeductionIncomeThresholdSingle" /></Then>
          </Case>
        </Switch>
      </Derived>
    </Fact>

    <Fact path="/vaAgeDeductionReduction">
      <Name>Age deduction reduction</Name>
      <Description>Va. Code § 58.1-322.03(5)(b): $1 for each $1 of AFAGI over the threshold, never
        below zero. 2024 Form 760 instructions, Age Deduction Worksheet line 11. One figure for the
        return; on a joint return it applies to each spouse's $12,000.</Description>
      <Derived>
        <GreaterOf>
          <Dollar>0</Dollar>
          <Subtract>
            <Minuend><Dependency path="/vaAdjustedFederalAdjustedGrossIncome" /></Minuend>
            <Subtrahends><Dependency path="/vaAgeDeductionIncomeThreshold" /></Subtrahends>
          </Subtract>
        </GreaterOf>
      </Derived>
    </Fact>

    <Fact path="/vaPrimaryFilerAgeDeductionAllowed">
      <Name>Age deduction the primary filer qualifies for</Name>
      <Description>Va. Code § 58.1-322.03(5): $12,000 if born on or before January 1, 1939;
        otherwise, if 65 or older, $12,000 reduced by the income-based reduction, never below zero;
        otherwise $0. The disability subtraction that can be taken instead is out of scope.</Description>
      <Derived>
        <Switch>
          <Case>
            <When><Dependency path="/vaPrimaryFilerBornOnOrBefore1939" /></When>
            <Then><Dependency module="virginiaConstants" path="/vaAgeDeductionMaximum" /></Then>
          </Case>
          <Case>
            <When><Dependency path="/vaPrimaryFilerQualifiesForIncomeBasedAgeDeduction" /></When>
            <Then>
              <GreaterOf>
                <Dollar>0</Dollar>
                <Subtract>
                  <Minuend><Dependency module="virginiaConstants" path="/vaAgeDeductionMaximum" /></Minuend>
                  <Subtrahends><Dependency path="/vaAgeDeductionReduction" /></Subtrahends>
                </Subtract>
              </GreaterOf>
            </Then>
          </Case>
          <Case>
            <When><True /></When>
            <Then><Dollar>0</Dollar></Then>
          </Case>
        </Switch>
      </Derived>
    </Fact>

    <Fact path="/vaSpouseAgeDeductionAllowed">
      <Name>Age deduction the spouse qualifies for</Name>
      <Description>Va. Code § 58.1-322.03(5), for the spouse on a joint return, with the same rule as
        the primary filer: $12,000 if born on or before January 1, 1939; otherwise, if 65 or older,
        $12,000 reduced by the return's income-based reduction; otherwise $0. Assumption, from the
        Code's text: the deduction is "for individuals", and on a joint return "the taxpayer's
        adjusted federal adjusted gross income" is the joint AFAGI, so each spouse's $12,000 is
        reduced by the same excess over $75,000. If Virginia Tax's Age Deduction Worksheet instead
        reduces the couple's combined $24,000 once, this is the fact to change.</Description>
      <Derived>
        <Switch>
          <Case>
            <When><Dependency module="virginiaFiler" path="/vaSpouseBornOnOrBefore1939" /></When>
            <Then><Dependency module="virginiaConstants" path="/vaAgeDeductionMaximum" /></Then>
          </Case>
          <Case>
            <When><Dependency path="/vaSpouseQualifiesForIncomeBasedAgeDeduction" /></When>
            <Then>
              <GreaterOf>
                <Dollar>0</Dollar>
                <Subtract>
                  <Minuend><Dependency module="virginiaConstants" path="/vaAgeDeductionMaximum" /></Minuend>
                  <Subtrahends><Dependency path="/vaAgeDeductionReduction" /></Subtrahends>
                </Subtract>
              </GreaterOf>
            </Then>
          </Case>
          <Case>
            <When><True /></When>
            <Then><Dollar>0</Dollar></Then>
          </Case>
        </Switch>
      </Derived>
    </Fact>

    <Fact path="/vaAgeDeductionAllowed">
      <Name>Age deduction the return qualifies for</Name>
      <Description>Va. Code § 58.1-322.03(5): the primary filer's deduction plus, on a joint return,
        the spouse's. Line 4 claims this unless the return claims a low-income credit instead
        (/vaClaimsLowIncomeCredit). 2024 Form 760 instructions, Line 4 and the Age Deduction
        Worksheet.</Description>
      <Derived>
        <Add>
          <Dependency path="/vaPrimaryFilerAgeDeductionAllowed" />
          <Dependency path="/vaSpouseAgeDeductionAllowed" />
        </Add>
      </Derived>
    </Fact>

    <Fact path="/vaAgeDeduction">
      <Name>Form 760 Line 4, age deduction</Name>
      <Description>Va. Code § 58.1-339.8(D)(5): a return on which the filer or the spouse claims the age
        deduction cannot claim the Credit for Low-Income Individuals or either Virginia Earned Income
        Credit. The age deduction the return qualifies for, or $0 when the return claims one of those
        credits instead.</Description>
      <Derived>
        <Switch>
          <Case>
            <When><Dependency module="virginiaCredits" path="/vaClaimsLowIncomeCredit" /></When>
            <Then><Dollar>0</Dollar></Then>
          </Case>
          <Case>
            <When><True /></When>
            <Then><Dependency path="/vaAgeDeductionAllowed" /></Then>
          </Case>
        </Switch>
      </Derived>
    </Fact>

    <Fact path="/vaHasMilitaryIncome">
      <Name>Served in, or received retirement pay from, the U.S. Armed Forces in 2024</Name>
      <Description>Asked, as the gate to the two military questions. Neither basic pay nor military
        retirement is identifiable on the forms the federal return exports: a W-2 from the military
        reports box 1, not basic pay, and the federal 1099-R question "is this from a military
        retirement plan" is not exported to states.</Description>
      <Writable><Boolean /></Writable>
    </Fact>

    <Fact path="/vaHasMilitaryBasicPay">
      <Name>On extended active duty for more than 90 consecutive days in 2024</Name>
      <Description>Va. Code § 58.1-322.02(15). Asked; primary filer only.</Description>
      <Writable><Boolean /></Writable>
    </Fact>

    <Fact path="/vaMilitaryBasicPay">
      <Name>Military basic pay received in 2024</Name>
      <Description>Basic pay only, from the filer's Leave and Earnings Statements; not allowances,
        bonuses or special pays, which W-2 box 1 also includes.</Description>
      <Writable><Dollar /></Writable>
      <Placeholder><Dollar>0</Dollar></Placeholder>
    </Fact>

    <Fact path="/vaMilitaryBasicPaySubtractionAllowed">
      <Name>Military basic pay subtraction the filer qualifies for (Schedule ADJ code 38)</Name>
      <Description>Va. Code § 58.1-322.02(15): all basic pay up to $15,000; above that, $15,000
        reduced dollar for dollar by the pay over $15,000, so nothing at $30,000 or more. Limited to
        what federal AGI includes, here W-2 wages. The cap is the household's /wages (exported to
        MeF): the federal per-filer figures (/primaryFilerWages, /formW2s/*/filer,
        /formW2s/*/belongsToPrimaryFiler) are not exported to states, so the primary filer's own
        wages cannot be read here; on a joint return the cap is therefore loose by the spouse's
        wages. Claimed on Line 7 only if the return does not claim a low-income credit (Va. Code
        § 58.1-339.8(D)(2)).</Description>
      <Derived>
        <Switch>
          <Case>
            <When><Not><Dependency path="/vaHasMilitaryIncome" /></Not></When>
            <Then><Dollar>0</Dollar></Then>
          </Case>
          <Case>
            <When><Not><Dependency path="/vaHasMilitaryBasicPay" /></Not></When>
            <Then><Dollar>0</Dollar></Then>
          </Case>
          <Case>
            <When>
              <LessThanOrEqual>
                <Left><Dependency path="/vaMilitaryBasicPay" /></Left>
                <Right><Dependency module="virginiaConstants" path="/vaMilitaryBasicPayMaximum" /></Right>
              </LessThanOrEqual>
            </When>
            <Then>
              <LesserOf>
                <Dependency path="/vaMilitaryBasicPay" />
                <Dependency module="formW2s" path="/wages" />
              </LesserOf>
            </Then>
          </Case>
          <Case>
            <When><True /></When>
            <Then>
              <LesserOf>
                <Dependency module="formW2s" path="/wages" />
                <Dependency path="/vaMilitaryBasicPayPhasedOut" />
              </LesserOf>
            </Then>
          </Case>
        </Switch>
      </Derived>
    </Fact>

    <Fact path="/vaMilitaryBasicPayPhasedOut">
      <Name>Military basic pay subtraction after the phase-out</Name>
      <Description>Va. Code § 58.1-322.02(15): $15,000 reduced $1 for each $1 of basic pay over
        $15,000, never below zero. Only read when the basic pay is over $15,000.</Description>
      <Derived>
        <GreaterOf>
          <Dollar>0</Dollar>
          <Subtract>
            <Minuend><Dependency module="virginiaConstants" path="/vaMilitaryBasicPayMaximum" /></Minuend>
            <Subtrahends>
              <Subtract>
                <Minuend><Dependency path="/vaMilitaryBasicPay" /></Minuend>
                <Subtrahends><Dependency module="virginiaConstants" path="/vaMilitaryBasicPayMaximum" /></Subtrahends>
              </Subtract>
            </Subtrahends>
          </Subtract>
        </GreaterOf>
      </Derived>
    </Fact>

    <Fact path="/vaMilitaryBasicPaySubtraction">
      <Name>Schedule ADJ code 38, military basic pay subtraction, as claimed</Name>
      <Description>The subtraction the filer qualifies for, or $0 when the return claims a low-income
        credit instead (Va. Code § 58.1-339.8(D)(2)).</Description>
      <Derived>
        <Switch>
          <Case>
            <When><Dependency module="virginiaCredits" path="/vaClaimsLowIncomeCredit" /></When>
            <Then><Dollar>0</Dollar></Then>
          </Case>
          <Case>
            <When><True /></When>
            <Then><Dependency path="/vaMilitaryBasicPaySubtractionAllowed" /></Then>
          </Case>
        </Switch>
      </Derived>
    </Fact>

    <Fact path="/vaHasMilitaryRetirement">
      <Name>Received military retirement pay or Survivor Benefit Plan payments in 2024</Name>
      <Description>Va. Code § 58.1-322.02(18)(c) and (d). Asked; primary filer only.</Description>
      <Writable><Boolean /></Writable>
    </Fact>

    <Fact path="/vaMilitaryRetirementIncome">
      <Name>Military benefits received in 2024</Name>
      <Description>The taxable amount (1099-R box 2a) of military retirement pay, Survivor Benefit
        Plan payments and other military benefits paid to a surviving spouse.</Description>
      <Writable><Dollar /></Writable>
      <Placeholder><Dollar>0</Dollar></Placeholder>
    </Fact>

    <Fact path="/vaForm1099RTaxableAmounts">
      <Name>Taxable amount on every 1099-R of the return</Name>
      <Description>The sum of box 2a across the 1099-Rs on the federal return
        (/form1099Rs/*/taxableAmount, exported to MeF in each 1099-R). Military benefits are
        retirement income, so a military benefits subtraction cannot exceed this.</Description>
      <Derived>
        <CollectionSum>
          <Dependency module="form1099Rs" path="/form1099Rs/*/taxableAmount" />
        </CollectionSum>
      </Derived>
    </Fact>

    <Fact path="/vaMilitaryBenefitsSubtraction">
      <Name>Schedule ADJ code 60, military benefits subtraction</Name>
      <Description>Va. Code § 58.1-322.02(18)(c): up to $30,000 for taxable year 2024, at any age, and
        never more than the taxable 1099-R income the federal return reports (the subtraction is of an
        amount "included therein", in federal AGI). It does not bar the low-income credits
        (§ 58.1-339.8(D) does not list it).</Description>
      <Derived>
        <Switch>
          <Case>
            <When><Not><Dependency path="/vaHasMilitaryIncome" /></Not></When>
            <Then><Dollar>0</Dollar></Then>
          </Case>
          <Case>
            <When><Dependency path="/vaHasMilitaryRetirement" /></When>
            <Then>
              <LesserOf>
                <Dependency path="/vaMilitaryRetirementIncome" />
                <Dependency module="virginiaConstants" path="/vaMilitaryBenefitsMaximum" />
                <Dependency path="/vaForm1099RTaxableAmounts" />
              </LesserOf>
            </Then>
          </Case>
          <Case>
            <When><True /></When>
            <Then><Dollar>0</Dollar></Then>
          </Case>
        </Switch>
      </Derived>
    </Fact>

    <Fact path="/vaUnemploymentCompensationSubtraction">
      <Name>Schedule ADJ code 37, unemployment benefits subtraction</Name>
      <Description>Va. Code § 58.1-322.02: unemployment compensation included in federal AGI is
        subtracted in full (2024 Form 760 instructions, Schedule ADJ subtraction code 37). Direct File
        puts each 1099-G's box 1 into AGI net of what was repaid in the year, and exports both figures
        to states (/form1099Gs/*/amount, /form1099Gs/*/amountPaidBackForBenefitsInTaxYear), so the
        subtraction is their difference, rounded the way the federal /unemploymentCompensation is. No
        question is asked.</Description>
      <Derived>
        <Round>
          <Subtract>
            <Minuend>
              <CollectionSum>
                <Dependency module="unemployment" path="/form1099Gs/*/amount" />
              </CollectionSum>
            </Minuend>
            <Subtrahends>
              <CollectionSum>
                <Dependency module="unemployment" path="/form1099Gs/*/amountPaidBackForBenefitsInTaxYear" />
              </CollectionSum>
            </Subtrahends>
          </Subtract>
        </Round>
      </Derived>
    </Fact>

    <!-- The Virginia Lottery subtraction (Schedule ADJ code 24) is deliberately absent. Va. Code
         § 58.1-322.02(7) subtracts only "any amount included therein", in federal AGI, "less than
         $600 from a prize awarded by the Virginia Lottery". Direct File has no gambling or other-income
         fact, so no prize is ever in Line 1, and a filer with such income is outside Direct File's
         scope; a question about it could only subtract what was never added. -->

    <Fact path="/vaScheduleAdjSubtractions">
      <Name>Form 760 Line 7, subtractions from Schedule ADJ</Name>
      <Description>Schedule ADJ Line 7: unemployment benefits (code 37), military basic pay (code 38)
        as claimed, and military benefits (code 60). The other Schedule ADJ subtractions are out of
        scope and taken as $0.</Description>
      <Derived>
        <Add>
          <Dependency path="/vaUnemploymentCompensationSubtraction" />
          <Dependency path="/vaMilitaryBasicPaySubtraction" />
          <Dependency path="/vaMilitaryBenefitsSubtraction" />
        </Add>
      </Derived>
    </Fact>

    <Fact path="/vaSubtractionsEitherWay">
      <Name>Subtractions the low-income credits do not affect</Name>
      <Description>Line 5 (Social Security), and on Line 7 the unemployment and military benefits
        subtractions. The age deduction and the military basic pay subtraction are the two that a
        low-income credit replaces.</Description>
      <Derived>
        <Add>
          <Dependency path="/vaTaxableSocialSecurityBenefits" />
          <Dependency path="/vaUnemploymentCompensationSubtraction" />
          <Dependency path="/vaMilitaryBenefitsSubtraction" />
        </Add>
      </Derived>
    </Fact>

    <Fact path="/vaWithoutCreditTotalSubtractions">
      <Name>Line 8 if the return keeps the age deduction and military basic pay subtraction</Name>
      <Description>Lines 4 + 5 + 6 + 7 with Line 4 and code 38 as the filers qualify for them. Line 6
        (state income tax refund, Va. Code § 58.1-322.02(5)) is out of scope and taken as $0.</Description>
      <Derived>
        <Add>
          <Dependency path="/vaSubtractionsEitherWay" />
          <Dependency path="/vaAgeDeductionAllowed" />
          <Dependency path="/vaMilitaryBasicPaySubtractionAllowed" />
        </Add>
      </Derived>
    </Fact>

    <Fact path="/vaWithCreditTotalSubtractions">
      <Name>Line 8 if the return claims a low-income credit</Name>
      <Description>Lines 5 + 7 with no age deduction and no military basic pay subtraction (Va. Code
        § 58.1-339.8(D)(2) and (5)).</Description>
      <Derived><Dependency path="/vaSubtractionsEitherWay" /></Derived>
    </Fact>

    <Fact path="/vaWithoutCreditAdjustedGrossIncome">
      <Name>Line 9 if the return keeps the age deduction and military basic pay subtraction</Name>
      <Description>Line 1 minus Line 8, with Line 4 and code 38 as the filers qualify for them.</Description>
      <Derived>
        <Subtract>
          <Minuend><Dependency path="/vaFederalAdjustedGrossIncome" /></Minuend>
          <Subtrahends><Dependency path="/vaWithoutCreditTotalSubtractions" /></Subtrahends>
        </Subtract>
      </Derived>
    </Fact>

    <Fact path="/vaWithCreditAdjustedGrossIncome">
      <Name>Line 9 if the return claims a low-income credit</Name>
      <Description>Line 1 minus Line 8 with no age deduction and no military basic pay subtraction
        (Va. Code § 58.1-339.8(D)(2) and (5)). This is also the family VAGI of Schedule ADJ Line 10.</Description>
      <Derived>
        <Subtract>
          <Minuend><Dependency path="/vaFederalAdjustedGrossIncome" /></Minuend>
          <Subtrahends><Dependency path="/vaWithCreditTotalSubtractions" /></Subtrahends>
        </Subtract>
      </Derived>
    </Fact>

    <Fact path="/vaTotalSubtractions">
      <Name>Form 760 Line 8, total subtractions</Name>
      <Description>Lines 4 + 5 + 6 + 7, as claimed: the with-credit or the without-credit figure,
        whichever way the return files, so that Line 9 is always Line 1 minus this.</Description>
      <Derived>
        <Switch>
          <Case>
            <When><Dependency module="virginiaCredits" path="/vaClaimsLowIncomeCredit" /></When>
            <Then><Dependency path="/vaWithCreditTotalSubtractions" /></Then>
          </Case>
          <Case>
            <When><True /></When>
            <Then><Dependency path="/vaWithoutCreditTotalSubtractions" /></Then>
          </Case>
        </Switch>
      </Derived>
    </Fact>

    <Fact path="/vaAdjustedGrossIncome">
      <Name>Form 760 Line 9, Virginia adjusted gross income</Name>
      <Description>Line 3 minus Line 8. Va. Code § 58.1-322 defines Virginia taxable income by
        reference to federal adjusted gross income with the Chapter 3 modifications.</Description>
      <Derived>
        <Switch>
          <Case>
            <When><Dependency module="virginiaCredits" path="/vaClaimsLowIncomeCredit" /></When>
            <Then><Dependency path="/vaWithCreditAdjustedGrossIncome" /></Then>
          </Case>
          <Case>
            <When><True /></When>
            <Then><Dependency path="/vaWithoutCreditAdjustedGrossIncome" /></Then>
          </Case>
        </Switch>
      </Derived>
    </Fact>

    <Fact path="/vaFilingThreshold">
      <Name>Virginia filing threshold for this return</Name>
      <Description>Va. Code § 58.1-321(A).</Description>
      <Derived>
        <Switch>
          <Case>
            <When><Dependency module="virginiaFiler" path="/vaIsFilingStatus2" /></When>
            <Then><Dependency module="virginiaConstants" path="/vaFilingThresholdMarried" /></Then>
          </Case>
          <Case>
            <When><True /></When>
            <Then><Dependency module="virginiaConstants" path="/vaFilingThresholdSingle" /></Then>
          </Case>
        </Switch>
      </Derived>
    </Fact>

    <Fact path="/vaWithoutCreditIsBelowFilingThreshold">
      <Name>Below the filing threshold, keeping the age deduction</Name>
      <Description>Va. Code § 58.1-321(A); 2024 Form 760 instructions, Line 9: if Line 9 is less
        than the amount for your filing status, your Virginia income tax is $0.</Description>
      <Derived>
        <LessThan>
          <Left><Dependency path="/vaWithoutCreditAdjustedGrossIncome" /></Left>
          <Right><Dependency path="/vaFilingThreshold" /></Right>
        </LessThan>
      </Derived>
    </Fact>

    <Fact path="/vaWithCreditIsBelowFilingThreshold">
      <Name>Below the filing threshold, claiming a low-income credit</Name>
      <Description>Va. Code § 58.1-321(A); 2024 Form 760 instructions, Line 9: if Line 9 is less
        than the amount for your filing status, your Virginia income tax is $0.</Description>
      <Derived>
        <LessThan>
          <Left><Dependency path="/vaWithCreditAdjustedGrossIncome" /></Left>
          <Right><Dependency path="/vaFilingThreshold" /></Right>
        </LessThan>
      </Derived>
    </Fact>

    <Fact path="/vaIsBelowFilingThreshold">
      <Name>Virginia adjusted gross income below the filing threshold</Name>
      <Description>Va. Code § 58.1-321(A); 2024 Form 760 instructions, Line 9: if Line 9 is less
        than the amount for your filing status, your Virginia income tax is $0. The with-credit or
        the without-credit test, whichever way the return files.</Description>
      <Derived>
        <Switch>
          <Case>
            <When><Dependency module="virginiaCredits" path="/vaClaimsLowIncomeCredit" /></When>
            <Then><Dependency path="/vaWithCreditIsBelowFilingThreshold" /></Then>
          </Case>
          <Case>
            <When><True /></When>
            <Then><Dependency path="/vaWithoutCreditIsBelowFilingThreshold" /></Then>
          </Case>
        </Switch>
      </Derived>
    </Fact>

  </Facts>
