<?xml-model href="./FactDictionaryModule.rng"?>
<!--
  Virginia resident return, tax year 2024: prototype rules, not a return. One of the Virginia
  modules (facts/virginia*.xml), loaded as one dictionary beside the federal modules; the
  Virginia README in docs/virginia/ lists them and docs/adr/003-the-layout-for-growth.md says
  why they are split. Every fact names its source: Va. Code Title 58.1, Chapter 3
  (https://law.lis.virginia.gov/vacode/title58.1/) and the 2024 Form 760 instructions. A module
  reads federal facts only through what the federal return exports to states
  (stateSystems="true") or to MeF (mef="true"); scripts/check-virginia-exports.py enforces it.

  This module: Lines 19a to 28: withholding from the W-2s whose MeF state code names Virginia, the
  three payments Virginia Tax's own records hold (writable, filled by the records stand-in on the
  page), the total paid, and the tax owed or overpaid.
-->
<FactDictionaryModule>
  <Facts>



    <!-- ============ Lines 19a to 28: what has already been paid, and the result. ============ -->

    <Fact path="/formW2s/*/vaStateIsVirginia">
      <Name>This W-2's box 15 names Virginia</Name>
      <Description>Direct File derives each W-2's MeF state code (/formW2s/*/xmlStateCd, the
        StateAbbreviationCd of the W-2 in the Form 1040 XML a state receives) from the residence
        answer whenever box 15 is filled in, and knocks a return out when a W-2 is from another state
        (/flowKnockoutBox15IncomeFromDifferentState); the box 15 answer itself (/formW2s/*/state) is
        not exported. So on a Virginia resident return the code is "VA" exactly when box 15 is
        filled in, and that is the test here: a resident return and a state code present. Written
        as a completeness test rather than a comparison with "VA" because the workbench sandbox stands
        each federal fact in by type and has no per-form string; the two tests agree on every return
        this module can see, and the ScalaTest asserts the stricter one.</Description>
      <Derived>
        <All>
          <Dependency module="virginiaFiler" path="/vaIsResident" />
          <IsComplete><Dependency module="formW2s" path="../xmlStateCd" /></IsComplete>
        </All>
      </Derived>
    </Fact>

    <Fact path="/formW2s/*/vaWithholding">
      <Name>This W-2's Virginia income tax withheld</Name>
      <Description>Box 17 (/formW2s/*/stateWithholding, exported to MeF in each W-2) when box 15 names
        Virginia; otherwise $0.</Description>
      <Derived>
        <Switch>
          <Case>
            <When><Dependency path="../vaStateIsVirginia" /></When>
            <Then><Dependency module="formW2s" path="../stateWithholding" /></Then>
          </Case>
          <Case>
            <When><True /></When>
            <Then><Dollar>0</Dollar></Then>
          </Case>
        </Switch>
      </Derived>
    </Fact>

    <Fact path="/vaWithholding">
      <Name>Form 760 Line 19a, Virginia income tax withheld</Name>
      <Description>The sum of box 17 across the W-2s on the federal return whose box 15 names
        Virginia. The employer files the same W-2 with Virginia. Line 19b (the spouse's share on a
        joint return) is folded in here: which filer a W-2 belongs to (/formW2s/*/filer,
        /formW2s/*/belongsToPrimaryFiler) is not exported to states, so the split cannot be made
        from the export; a state would match each W-2's employee TIN (/formW2s/*/usedTin, exported)
        against the filers' TINs instead. Line 19 (19a + 19b) is unchanged by the split.</Description>
      <Derived>
        <CollectionSum>
          <Dependency path="/formW2s/*/vaWithholding" />
        </CollectionSum>
      </Derived>
    </Fact>

    <Fact path="/vaEstimatedPayments">
      <Name>Form 760 Line 20, estimated payments made for 2024</Name>
      <Description>Virginia Tax received these and holds the record; a state-run filer would fill this
        line from its own books. This prototype has no connection to those records, so the line is
        writable and defaults to $0.</Description>
      <Writable><Dollar /></Writable>
      <Placeholder><Dollar>0</Dollar></Placeholder>
    </Fact>

    <Fact path="/vaPriorYearOverpaymentApplied">
      <Name>Form 760 Line 21, last year's overpayment applied to 2024</Name>
      <Description>From Virginia Tax's own record of the 2023 return. Writable here, default $0, for the
        same reason as Line 20.</Description>
      <Writable><Dollar /></Writable>
      <Placeholder><Dollar>0</Dollar></Placeholder>
    </Fact>

    <Fact path="/vaExtensionPayments">
      <Name>Form 760 Line 22, extension payments</Name>
      <Description>Payments made with Form 760IP; Virginia Tax holds the record. Writable here, default
        $0.</Description>
      <Writable><Dollar /></Writable>
      <Placeholder><Dollar>0</Dollar></Placeholder>
    </Fact>

    <Fact path="/vaPaymentsMade">
      <Name>Form 760 Lines 19a to 22, tax withheld and paid</Name>
      <Description>Withholding plus the payments Virginia Tax holds a record of.</Description>
      <Derived>
        <Add>
          <Dependency path="/vaWithholding" />
          <Dependency path="/vaEstimatedPayments" />
          <Dependency path="/vaPriorYearOverpaymentApplied" />
          <Dependency path="/vaExtensionPayments" />
        </Add>
      </Derived>
    </Fact>

    <Fact path="/vaTotalPayments">
      <Name>Form 760 Line 26, total payments and credits</Name>
      <Description>Lines 19a to 25. Lines 24 and 25 (credit for tax paid to another state, Schedule
        CR credits) are out of scope and taken as $0.</Description>
      <Derived>
        <Add>
          <Dependency path="/vaPaymentsMade" />
          <Dependency module="virginiaCredits" path="/vaLowIncomeCredit" />
        </Add>
      </Derived>
    </Fact>

    <Fact path="/vaTaxYouOwe">
      <Name>Form 760 Line 27, tax you owe before use tax</Name>
      <Description>Line 18 minus Line 26 when positive. Line 17 (the spouse tax adjustment) is out of
        scope, so Line 18 equals Line 16.</Description>
      <Derived>
        <GreaterOf>
          <Dollar>0</Dollar>
          <Subtract>
            <Minuend><Dependency module="virginiaTax" path="/vaTax" /></Minuend>
            <Subtrahends><Dependency path="/vaTotalPayments" /></Subtrahends>
          </Subtract>
        </GreaterOf>
      </Derived>
    </Fact>

    <Fact path="/vaOverpayment">
      <Name>Form 760 Line 28, your tax overpayment</Name>
      <Description>Line 26 minus Line 18 when positive.</Description>
      <Derived>
        <GreaterOf>
          <Dollar>0</Dollar>
          <Subtract>
            <Minuend><Dependency path="/vaTotalPayments" /></Minuend>
            <Subtrahends><Dependency module="virginiaTax" path="/vaTax" /></Subtrahends>
          </Subtract>
        </GreaterOf>
      </Derived>
    </Fact>

  </Facts>
</FactDictionaryModule>

  refunded.
-->
<FactDictionaryModule>
  <Facts>


    <!-- ============ Line 33, the question every Virginian is asked, and Lines 35 and 36. ============ -->

    <Fact path="/vaHasUntaxedPurchases">
      <Name>Bought something in 2024 without paying Virginia sales tax</Name>
      <Description>Online, by mail or out of state, where the seller charged no Virginia tax. Form 760
        Line 33 (consumer's use tax); no seller reports it, so the filer is asked. The form also has an
        oval to fill when no use tax is due.</Description>
      <Writable><Boolean /></Writable>
    </Fact>

    <Fact path="/vaUntaxedPurchases">
      <Name>Total of purchases on which no Virginia sales tax was paid</Name>
      <Description>2024 Form 760 instructions, Line 33: the instructions offer a lookup table for totals
        under $1,000 and a worksheet above that; this prototype applies the rate directly.</Description>
      <Writable><Dollar /></Writable>
      <Placeholder><Dollar>0</Dollar></Placeholder>
    </Fact>

    <Fact path="/vaUseTax">
      <Name>Form 760 Line 33, consumer's use tax</Name>
      <Description>The untaxed purchases times the rate for the filer's locality
        (/vaUseTaxRate in the virginiaLocalities module), rounded to the dollar; $0 when the filer had
        no untaxed purchases.</Description>
      <Derived>
        <Switch>
          <Case>
            <When><Dependency path="/vaHasUntaxedPurchases" /></When>
            <Then>
              <Round>
                <Multiply>
                  <Dependency module="virginiaLocalities" path="/vaUseTaxRate" />
                  <Dependency path="/vaUntaxedPurchases" />
                </Multiply>
              </Round>
            </Then>
          </Case>
          <Case>
            <When><True /></When>
            <Then><Dollar>0</Dollar></Then>
          </Case>
        </Switch>
      </Derived>
    </Fact>

    <Fact path="/vaAmountYouOwe">
      <Name>Form 760 Line 35, amount you owe</Name>
      <Description>Line 27 plus Line 34 when there is tax owed; otherwise Line 34 less the overpayment on
        Line 28 when that is positive. Line 34 here is the use tax alone: Lines 29 to 32 (overpayment
        credited to next year, voluntary contributions, penalty and interest) are out of scope.</Description>
      <Derived>
        <GreaterOf>
          <Dollar>0</Dollar>
          <Subtract>
            <Minuend>
              <Add>
                <Dependency module="virginiaPayments" path="/vaTaxYouOwe" />
                <Dependency path="/vaUseTax" />
              </Add>
            </Minuend>
            <Subtrahends><Dependency module="virginiaPayments" path="/vaOverpayment" /></Subtrahends>
          </Subtract>
        </GreaterOf>
      </Derived>
    </Fact>

    <Fact path="/vaRefund">

      <Description>Line 28 less Line 34 when positive.</Description>
      <Derived>
        <GreaterOf>
          <Dollar>0</Dollar>
          <Subtract>
            <Minuend><Dependency module="virginiaPayments" path="/vaOverpayment" /></Minuend>
            <Subtrahends><Dependency path="/vaUseTax" /></Subtrahends>

$comment: The federal facts the Virginia module reads, as the workbench's sandbox stands them in.
The workbench does not load the 36 federal modules. It loads virginia.xml and
virginiaLocalities.xml beside one writable stand-in for each federal fact listed here, so a
worked example can say 'federal AGI is $40,000' instead of building a W-2 and a 1040 to get
there. That is ADR-001's integration rule made literal: Virginia may read only what the federal
return hands to states, and this file is that list.
When virginia.xml starts depending on a federal fact that is not here, `node workbench/check.mjs`
fails and names it. Adding it is an engineering task: one entry here, with its type.
Types: dollar, boolean, day, enum (with options), count (a collection of N items whose one
field is true), dollarList (a collection with one dollar field per item).
One thing the sandbox cannot do yet, and the entry that waits on it:
- The spouse is settable: /vaSpouse/age65OrOlder, /vaSpouse/isBlind and /vaSpouse/dateOfBirth are
the second filer's /filers/*/age65OrOlder, isBlind and dateOfBirth, read through virginiaFiler.xml's
/vaSpouse (the filer whose exported isPrimaryFiler is false); lib/sandbox.js maps the /vaSpouse/
(or /secondaryFiler/) prefix onto the second filer's item the way it maps /primaryFiler/.
- Box 15 of each W-2. /formW2s/*/xmlStateCd is the W-2's state code in the MeF XML, a string;
virginia.xml tests only whether it is present (on a Virginia resident return it is then VA).
The sandbox has no per-form string, so it is stood in as a count: the first N W-2s carry a state
code and the rest have a blank box 15. Keep it listed before /formW2s/*/stateWithholding, whose
list sets the number of W-2s.
- Two lists on one collection must have the same length: give /form1099Gs/*/amountPaidBackForBenefitsInTaxYear
one entry per 1099-G, 0 when nothing was repaid.
- /taxYear is an int: the season the site is built for (constants.xml). Values that change by year are written as a Switch on it, so an example for a later year sets it.
- A count left out of an example means every item: each W-2 carries a state code unless the example says how many do.

$comment: Worked examples for the Virginia return: a household, and what the law says some of its lines must be.
Authored here, not in scenarios/ (which `make export-scenarios` regenerates). `baseline` is the answer every
example starts from; an example lists only what differs. Paths in `inputs` are fact paths: Virginia's own
questions, or the federal stand-ins in ../federal-inputs.json.
Checked two ways when written: by the engine, and by the independent model of the rules in
scripts/lib/virginia-model.cjs, written from the Code of Virginia rather than from virginia.xml. They agreed on
every line. Edit through the workbench, so a change to an expected answer goes through review like a rule does.
Run them: node workbench/check.mjs

of W-2s unless an example is about a W-2 from nowhere. A spouse's facts cannot be set here yet (see
../federal-inputs.json), so a joint return's spouse is under 65 and sighted in every example.
